comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 150-ECTS Mathematics major and 30-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation, instantiated with First-year Project Mathematics because it directly represents the named degree. The second- and third-year major contributes 90 ECTS. Dynamical Systems and Algebraic Structures are selected as the first two options in their regulated choice group; Project Statistical Reasoning is selected as the first option in the subsequent group; and Project Systems Theory is the first listed eligible elective. These choices are fixed by official order independently of UCR fit. The genuine 30-ECTS minor remains open rather than being populated with invented courses. Rechecked against the current official programme and 2026–2027 regulations on 2026-10-14; the settled 180-ECTS reconstruction and neutral choices are unchanged.
components: The project specific to the named Mathematics degree is selected from the regulated first-year choice.

alternatives.label: Mathematical methods, algorithms & autonomous systems
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is weighted toward calculus, linear algebra, numerical mathematics, probability, algorithms, optimisation and autonomous computational systems. It does not claim the target’s proof-based pure-mathematics spine.
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical methods, discrete structures, probability, numerical computation, algorithms, optimisation, machine learning and autonomous-system modelling. This is the strongest bounded mathematics-and-computation response, not a Mathematics degree.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Year-1 PPD and eight level-300 courses. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede all dependent computing and mathematics courses; all offerings match the six Fall-2026-cohort terms.

alternatives.label: Probability, statistical modelling & computational research
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum emphasises probability, inference, multivariate statistics, econometrics, Monte Carlo simulation, machine learning, research design and meta-analysis, with mathematics and programming as foundations.
alternatives.concept: Develop probability, statistical modelling, research design, econometrics, machine learning, numerical methods and reproducible computational research. This is a distinct quantitative-statistics route grounded in the target’s explicit probability interest and statistical curriculum.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with Alternative 1, this route replaces AI ethics, image processing, robotics, optimisation and reinforcement learning with research methods and statistics, empirical domain preparation, software development, econometrics and meta-analysis: five courses (37.5 EC) on each side are unique.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Year-1 PPD and seven level-300 courses. Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics, Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics, Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Advanced Research Seminar, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Probability, statistical modelling and computational research
Pure proof-based structures and advanced analysis

blocks: Both address professional and societal responsibility; UCR PPD is general formation rather than mathematics-specific ethics.
Both develop statistical modelling; UCR applies multivariate models in behavioural research rather than mathematical statistics.
Both develop programming for problem-solving; UCR teaches general Python rather than a mathematics-specific scientific-programming course.
Both use logic, sets and discrete structures; UCR applies them to algorithms rather than providing the full proof-based target course.
Both establish calculus and equation-solving foundations; UCR also introduces complex numbers and differential equations.
Both directly study systems, vectors, matrices and linear spaces; Groningen continues to a second dedicated course.
Both establish probability distributions; UCR combines probability with statistical inference and simulation.
Both study numerical root-finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential-equation methods with attention to error.
Both analyse linear systems through transforms, differential equations and state-space representations.
Both extend calculus; UCR includes multivariable and complex-valued functions but not the target analysis sequence.
Disciplinary requirements not reproduced at UCR

selection.assessment: The historical no-match judgment imposed full disciplinary equivalence. The strongest feasible response is a mathematics-and-computation curriculum, and the explicit probability interest supports one genuinely different statistical-research route. A third pure-mathematics direction was assessed but cannot form a complete UCR programme because the workbook lacks the target’s proof sequence in real and functional analysis, topology, group theory, geometry, number theory and advanced algebra, as well as comparable disciplinary project supervision. No further generator-eligible direction remains.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes are bounded related-field responses. They cover mathematical methods, computation, probability and quantitative research, but do not reproduce Groningen’s cumulative proof-based pure-mathematics curriculum in analysis, topology, group theory, geometry, number theory and algebraic structures or its 15-EC Mathematics research project.

All 151 current UCR workbook rows were reviewed from data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including descriptions, prerequisites and the exact six planned terms for the Fall 2026 cohort.
